extracted.intended_audience: GCC policymakers, national IP offices, legislators, judiciary, customs and enforcement bodies, and EU project stakeholders
extracted.subtask_description: A regional policy study providing a GAP analysis between EU best practices and current GCC IP regulatory frameworks, with concrete recommendations for harmonizing and improving copyright, trademarks, patents, designs, geographical indications, and enforcement. Aimed at guiding legal reform, capacity building, and treaty accession in GCC states.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design IP systems 'conducive to social and economic welfare'
rubrics_metrics.description: IP systems should be designed 'in a manner conducive to social and economic welfare, and to a balance of rights and obligations' (TRIPS objectives and principles).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The report emphasizes that design of IP rules must balance rewarding creativity with dissemination of knowledge; legislation should reflect country socio-economic needs and capacities and avoid 'TRIPS-plus' measures that harm local industry. New measures must be within the limits of a country’s human resources, legal and technical capacities and be accepted by affected sectors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measure IP system efficiency by acceptance and enforcement capacity
rubrics_metrics.description: The efficiency of an IP system is not measured by the level of protection in its laws and regulations but by its acceptance and adoption by the population and the capacity of national authorities to enforce it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before adopting higher protection levels, assess enforceability, public acceptance, and administrative/judicial capacity; emphasize outreach and stakeholder consultation (good governance and transparency).

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect TRIPS minimums and principles (NT, MFN, enforcement)
rubrics_metrics.description: GCC laws should comply with TRIPS minimum standards across Copyright, Related Rights, Trademarks, Industrial Designs, Patents, GIs, and Undisclosed Information and respect national treatment (NT) and most-favoured-nation (MFN) rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The report notes TRIPS does not replace existing conventions and that MFN and NT implications should be properly reflected in law (avoid reciprocal-only provisions). Implementation must consider TRIPS objectives and Doha Declaration on public health.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid adoption of 'alien' or non-contextual IP provisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not transpose IP provisions 'that do not respond to the market needs' or are 'alien' to the concerned population.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legislative reform should involve stakeholder consultation, transparency, and alignment with local market needs, to ensure acceptance and effective implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use TRIPS flexibilities for public health and access to knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: Use TRIPS flexibilities in designing IP policy to protect public health and access to knowledge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The report advises learning from EU and other experiences while ensuring policies leverage compulsory licensing and other TRIPS flexibilities where appropriate to serve socio-economic goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure transparency and stakeholder consultation in IP lawmaking
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopt principles of good governance and transparency when enacting IP legislation so affected sectors accept reforms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: public consultations (cited SAIP practice), stakeholder engagement, and impact assessment to increase legitimacy and effectiveness of new rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capacity building for IP examiners and administrative bodies
rubrics_metrics.description: Invest in capacity building of trademark examiners, patent professionals, IP offices, and enforcement officers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Improving substantive examination quality, reducing delays and costs, and harmonizing procedures depend on training and institutional strengthening; propose GCC IP Training Centre to conduct training and research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Build judicial IP expertise (specialized IP judges)
rubrics_metrics.description: Form a core group of specialized and competent national judges to handle IP matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specialized judiciary can provide practical, long-lasting solutions for costly and time-consuming infringement litigation and should be educated on IP principles and socio-economic impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Raise public and stakeholder IP awareness
rubrics_metrics.description: Raise IP awareness through campaigns and training for right holders, users, enforcement officers, and the judiciary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lack of awareness among rights holders and users is a key enforcement weakness; awareness campaigns should be national/regional and targeted (producers, customs, police, judiciary).

rubrics_metrics.name: Create IP enforcement coordination mechanisms (task forces)
rubrics_metrics.description: Create national IP task forces to coordinate enforcement cases, conduct joint raids and improve cross-agency cooperation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Task forces should include customs, police, IP offices, and prosecutors; coordination reduces duplication and improves enforcement outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish IP Enforcement Portal for data sharing
rubrics_metrics.description: Create an IP Enforcement Portal to enhance national coordination between right holders and enforcers for secure information sharing, data collection and enforcement analytics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Portal would inform about third-party infringements, consolidate enforcement data for policy analysis, and facilitate cooperation among stakeholders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revisit enforcement provisions to align with TRIPS (legal costs, harmonization, online remedies)
rubrics_metrics.description: Revisit enforcement provisions in IP laws to provide payment by the infringer of legal costs (as required by TRIPS), harmonize enforcement procedures and penalties, and introduce legal tools to combat online infringements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Modernize remedies, enable recovery of enforcement costs, ensure consistent penalties across statutes, and create specific online enforcement mechanisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create IP Units within Customs
rubrics_metrics.description: Create an IP Unit within Customs staffed by well-trained enforcement officers to stop counterfeiting and piracy at borders and coordinate with IP offices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unit responsibilities: monitor destruction of infringing goods, maintain databases of registered IP rights, cooperate with right holders, and exchange experience with other IP units internationally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide procedures to recover litigation costs and reduce litigation expense
rubrics_metrics.description: Address the high costs of infringement litigation by providing rights or procedures to recover litigation costs and by judicial reforms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim to make infringement litigation less costly and time-consuming through legal-cost awards, alternative dispute resolution, and judicial efficiency measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Introduce resale right (droit de suite) for original works of art
rubrics_metrics.description: Introduce a GCC unified law on 'resale right' or 'droit de suite' to benefit authors of original works of art and to preserve cultural works.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommended as a unified regional measure to support creators in the art market.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enhance protection of computer programs (decompilation/interoperability)
rubrics_metrics.description: Enhance protection of computer programs in GCC laws particularly regarding decompilation and interoperability exceptions/limits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance protection with interoperability needs; ensure national laws address decompilation and exceptions consistent with international practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protect non-original databases and advanced data processing systems
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide legal protection for non-original databases and advanced data processing systems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize value of databases even when originality is absent; consider sui generis database protection or other tailored regimes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Harmonize laws on protection of digital content
rubrics_metrics.description: Harmonize GCC laws relating to the protection of digital content across member states.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address digital-specific issues (TPM, rights management information), and consider accession to WIPO internet treaties (WCT, WPPT) and EU digital practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not extend general copyright term uniformly (protect public domain)
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid extending the general term of copyright protection across all GCC countries to preserve a strong public domain.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selective term policy recommended; balance incentives with public access and downstream uses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use EU experience to structure Collective Management Organizations (CMOs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use EU experience in CMOs to avoid misconceptions and build systems that benefit both users and right holders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop transparent governance, accountability, and efficient distribution mechanisms for CMOs; consider regional CMOs where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accede to Beijing Treaty and Marrakesh VIP Treaty
rubrics_metrics.description: Join the Beijing Treaty on Audiovisual Performances and the Marrakesh Treaty to improve protection of performers and access for persons with print disabilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bahrain, Kuwait and Oman specifically recommended to join Marrakesh; accession would align GCC with international norms on performers and accessibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bring national trademark laws into conformity with TRIPS
rubrics_metrics.description: Align national trademark laws with TRIPS requirements (examples: allow multiclass applications; adopt six-month grace period; provide national treatment).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: UAE: allow multiclass applications and six-month grace period; Qatar: amend reciprocity provisions to national treatment. Harmonization reduces barriers for national and foreign applicants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Define 'use' under trademark law
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a clear legal definition of 'use' under GCC trademark laws.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarity will reduce cancellation disputes for non-use and align practices with international standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invest in capacity building for trademark examiners and harmonize registration procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Improve substantive examination quality by training examiners and harmonizing registration procedures with international standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address criticisms of costly, time-consuming, and sometimes low-quality examination processes; capacity building should be regional and continuous.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accede to Singapore Treaty, Madrid Protocol, Nice and Vienna Agreements
rubrics_metrics.description: Adhere to procedural and classification treaties: Singapore Treaty, Madrid Protocol, Nice Classification, and Vienna Classification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accession will modernize procedural aspects, facilitate international filings, and harmonize classification systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adopt sui generis GI systems and create GI inventories/registries
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopt sui generis systems for Geographical Indications (GIs), establish inventories of potential GIs products and national/regional GI registries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Kuwait and UAE recommended to adopt sui generis systems; Oman already operational and a pilot for EU registration. EU can assist with inventories, producer associations, technical specifications and pilot projects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish GIs from PDOs/PGIs and study TSGs
rubrics_metrics.description: Differentiate between GIs and Protected Designations of Origin (PDOs) and Protected Geographical Indications (PGIs); study the need for Traditional Specialities Guaranteed (TSG).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Introduce PDOs/PGIs only when systems are mature; TSG study to evaluate necessity and suitability for GCC products.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide specific GI protections where appropriate (e.g., wines/spirits)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide additional GI protection for specific products (example: Oman to provide additional protection for wines and spirits).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tailor GI regimes to national product portfolios and policy choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit patents overbroad 'new uses' to protect generics
rubrics_metrics.description: Revisit patent provisions that extend protection to 'any new uses for, or new methods of using, a known product' to limit negative impacts on the generic pharmaceutical sector.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Oman specifically recommended to limit such provisions to avoid undue extension of patent scope affecting generics and access to medicines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider supplementary protection certificates carefully (pharmaceuticals)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use EU practice of Supplementary Protection Certificates (SPCs) cautiously to balance innovation incentives and local industry interests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Oman and Bahrain recommended to consider SPCs but with awareness of potential harm to local generic sectors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Align patent grace periods and maintenance fee rules with TRIPS
rubrics_metrics.description: Amend national rules on grace periods and fee payment/maintenance of industrial property rights to comply with TRIPS where currently inconsistent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Most GCC countries (except Bahrain and Oman) advised to amend grace-period provisions; ensure maintenance regimes do not inadvertently forfeit rights contrary to TRIPS obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide reversal of burden of proof for process patents (Article 34 TRIPS)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure laws provide for reversal of the burden of proof in respect of process patents where required by Article 34 of TRIPS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Kuwait, Qatar and the UAE urged to adopt such provisions to align with TRIPS; legislative change may affect enforcement and litigation strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibit discrimination between imported and locally produced patented products
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent laws should prohibit discrimination on whether products are imported or locally produced (national treatment obligations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Qatar and the UAE advised to update laws to prevent discrimination, aligning with TRIPS non-discrimination principles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accede to Budapest Treaty and Strasbourg Agreement
rubrics_metrics.description: Join international patent-related treaties such as the Budapest Treaty (deposit of microorganisms) and the Strasbourg Agreement (International Patent Classification).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Kuwait and UAE recommended for Budapest; all GCC countries encouraged to join classification treaties to facilitate examination and harmonization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improve patent work-sharing and validation agreements (PPH, PCT-PPH, SHARE, EPO validation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopt work-sharing modalities (Patent Prosecution Highway, PCT-PPH, SHARE) and consider validation agreements with the European Patent Office so EPO patents can have legal effect in GCC countries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work-sharing and validation can speed prosecution, improve examination quality, and reduce duplication; propose GCC Patent Office create specialized working groups to manage shared practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: GCC Patent Office to develop unified regulations and capacity building
rubrics_metrics.description: Have the GCC Patent Office create specialized working groups to develop unified regulations on matters affecting the common market and contribute to capacity building of patent professionals and SMEs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regional coordination is important for issues with cross-border market impact; the Office should also help SMEs with regional IP protection and commercialization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Broaden industrial design definitions and protections (including textiles)
rubrics_metrics.description: Improve the definition of industrial design to cover all categories and include special protection for textile designs as required by TRIPS Article 25.2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Modernize design laws to address challenges of the digital environment (e.g., 3D printing) and harmonize with international practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accede to Hague and Locarno design agreements
rubrics_metrics.description: Join the Hague Agreement (international registration of industrial designs) and the Locarno Agreement (international classification for industrial designs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accession facilitates international filings, harmonized classification, and international protection efficiency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support research, innovation and human capital for technology and science
rubrics_metrics.description: Support research and innovation in universities and research centres, fund innovative techniques, transfer and localize technology, and enhance the legislative and institutional framework to foster human capital.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement World Bank strategies: invest in early childhood, prepare better-educated/skilled youth, enable adult labor participation, and create enabling environments for human capital formation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess regulatory impacts on innovation before adoption
rubrics_metrics.description: Take into account the effect of each new initiative on innovation to ensure that policy and regulations support, rather than suppress, innovation and competitiveness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid rigid, overly detailed regulation that may hinder innovation; include innovation impact assessment in policymaking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop unified/regional laws where feasible (copyright digital, industrial designs, GIs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop unified GCC laws/regulations in targeted areas: a unified digital-environment copyright law, a unified industrial designs law, and a regional GI registry and legislation where appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Start with harmonized/regional frameworks for practical areas (digital copyright, designs) and consider unitary systems once capacity and harmonization prerequisites are met.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish a GCC Intellectual Property Training Centre
rubrics_metrics.description: Create a regional Training Centre to build capacity of IP professionals and academics, conduct research, and support harmonization efforts (regional CMOs, GI registry, unified designs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Centre to provide continuous professional development, promote best practices, and serve as repository for regional IP policy research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create inventories and pilot projects for GIs with EU technical support
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop inventories of potential GIs and run EU-supported pilot projects to prepare producer associations and technical specifications for GI registration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EU assistance recommended in preparing inventories and training producers; Oman and Saudi lists can be starting points.

rubrics_metrics.name: Harmonize enforcement procedures, provisional and border measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Harmonize provisional measures, border measures and remedies across trademark, customs and other IP laws to ensure consistent enforcement within the GCC common market.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include provisional measures under FTAs, GCC Unified Trademark Law, GCC Customs Law; ensure cross-border cooperation and data-sharing.
